'''''Helianthemum oelandicum''''', commonly called '''hoary rockrose''', is a low-growing plant confined to rocky dry calcareous areas especially close to the sea.

==Description==
[[Image:Hoary Rockrose plant.jpg|thumb|left|''H. oelandicum'' plant on [[The Burren]], [[Ireland]]]]
The plant typically has a central stock from which numerous branches radiate horizontally or ascending. Stipules are absent and the small leaves (about 10mm long) are simple and green above but densely hairy and grey below which is a distinguishing characteristic in areas where ''[[Helianthemum nummularium|H. nummularium]]'' is also present.<ref name="Stace"/>

The yellow flowers have 5 petals, free at the base and 5 sepals in [[Cyme (botany)|cymes]] generally with 1 to 6 flowers in each cyme.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book|title=New Flora of the British Isles|author=Stace C|publisher=Cambridge University Press|edition=second|date=2005|page=218|ISBN=0521427932}}</ref>

==Habitat==
It is restricted to dry limestone rocky areas. In Britain it is always close to the sea but in mainland Europe its range is restricted to the calcareous upland ranges such as the Alps.<ref>{{cite web|title=Helianthemum oelandicum|publisher =Kew Science - Plants of the World Online|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60461866-2|date=2016|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref>

==Distribution==
It occurs in several areas of [[Europe]] including [[France]], [[Germany]], [[Spain]], [[Sweden]] and parts of north [[Africa]] and the eastern [[Mediterranean]] countries. In the [[British Isles]] it is very restricted in its distribution being limited to parts of the South Wales coastline and a few locations on [[Anglesey]] and the [[Great Orme]].<ref name="Atlas">{{cite book|title=New Atlas of the British and Irish Flora|author1=Preston C. D.|author2= Pearman D. A.|author3= Dines T. D.|publisher=Oxford University Press|date=2003|ISBN=0198510675}}</ref>
